assertions.text: Table columns represent the method's public inputs (applicant type, age, claim count) and observable outputs (decision, premium) — not internal state like hasActivePolicy, internalRiskScore, or calculateRiskScore.
assertions.evidence: Columns: applicantType | age | claimCount | Status? | Premium? (inputs and outputs only)

assertions.text: No column is named after private fields or internal variables (hasActivePolicy, internalRiskScore, riskScore). The test treats the method as a black box.
assertions.evidence: All columns use public input names or observable output names; no private fields referenced

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column in both tables is 'Scenario' with entries like 'Renewal, no claims'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Applicant type', 'Age', 'Claims', 'Decision?', 'Premium?') — not code identifiers like 'applicantType', 'claimCount', 'String'.
assertions.evidence: Columns use code identifiers 'applicantType' and 'claimCount' instead of business language like 'Applicant Type' or 'Claims'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Renewal with no claims', 'Senior applicant') — not outcomes ('Auto approved', 'Rejected').
assertions.evidence: 'Renewal, no claims', 'High risk score', 'Senior applicant', 'Below senior threshold' describe conditions, not outcomes

assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Premium?')
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method bodies contain only assertAll() and assertEquals() calls; no if/switch statements present

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotation order is @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest for both methods, but @Description should not appear before @TableTest in standard JUnit order

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName("Application routing decisions") and @DisplayName("Premium tier selection") both present

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses triple-quoted strings ("""...""") for multi-line text, not concatenation

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules.
assertions.evidence: Two separate @TableTest methods: one for 'Application routing decisions', one for 'Premium tier selection'

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 has 5 rows, Table 2 has 5 rows covering boundaries; no unnecessary permutations visible

assertions.text: Decision logic (AUTO_APPROVED/REJECTED/APPROVED) and premium calculation are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: First table 'routesApplicationDecision' includes both Status? and Premium? columns; both concerns are tested in one method

assertions.text: Test method body does not recompute internal formulas (e.g. risk score calculation). It only calls the public API (evaluateApplication) and asserts on the return value's fields.
assertions.evidence: Test calls evaluateApplication() and asserts on getStatus() and getPremium(); no risk score calculation in test body

assertions.text: @Description explains the test's purpose and business context — not internal formulas or implementation details.
assertions.evidence: @Description includes 'Risk score = (age / 10) + (claimCount × 15). Rejection threshold is score > 75' which describes internal formulas

assertions.text: Approval decision table covers the rejection boundary thoroughly: 5 claims triggers rejection regardless of realistic age (risk score crosses 75), 4 claims results in approval.
assertions.evidence: Table shows 5 claims with REJECTED but no row with 4 claims to demonstrate the approval/rejection boundary cliff

assertions.text: Approved premium table covers boundary effects: the premium jump from 0 to 1 claim (impact of +15 risk score on premium), and the premium difference at age 64 vs 65 (standard vs senior formula).
assertions.evidence: Table 2 includes 'At senior threshold' (age 65, claimCount 0, Premium 221.0) and 'Below senior threshold' (age 64, claimCount 0, Premium 112.0) and rows with claimCount 0 vs 1
